Rule 1, Harassment: a post is harassment if it insults, mocks, or demeans a specific person or group of persons. Severity is low if the insult is mild and generic, medium if it targets a named member with ridicule or contempt, and high if it includes threats, slurs, or incitement.

Passage 1 — Successive discounts. When a first discount of p% is followed by a further discount of q% at the till, the price actually paid is the list price multiplied by (1 − p/100) and then by (1 − q/100). Each discount acts on the price that remains after the previous one, never on the original list price. Worked case: a 240-unit list price with 25% off followed by 10% off gives 240 × 0.75 = 180, then 180 × 0.90 = 162, so the till takes 162.

Passage 2 — Why the percentages cannot be added. A 25% discount followed by a 10% discount is not a 35% discount, because the second reduction acts on a smaller base. Computing with the list price alone, 200 × 0.75 = 150 and 150 × 0.90 = 135, whereas the mistaken combined method gives 200 × 0.65 = 130. The two methods never agree except when one discount is zero, so students must apply the discounts one at a time and in order.

Passage 3 — Checking by reversal. A discounted result can be checked by dividing by each factor in reverse order. If the final price F came from the list price L through factors (1 − p/100) and (1 − q/100), then F ÷ (1 − q/100) ÷ (1 − p/100) must return exactly L. If it does not, an arithmetic slip has occurred somewhere and the computation should be redone rather than adjusted by eye.

A1. THE FORGE AT EMBERFALL RIDGE. The forge has stood at the same spot on the Ridge for three hundred years, first raised by Dagan's grandfather's grandfather in the first winter after the Sundering, when the surviving townsfolk decided that if the autumn was going to be endless they would at least have nails. It has never been rebuilt, never relocated, never modernized. The bellows are second-generation; the anvil — 'the old anvil' — is first-generation and predates the court itself. Pilgrim guides routinely get this wrong, claiming some newer smithy stands at the ridge mouth; those are Kellwood's tents, not a forge. There is no other forge on the Ridge, in any patch, in any canon document, in any concept art. Idle line, patch 1.9: 'If it hasn't been rebuilt in three centuries, it isn't going to start for the likes of you.'

A2. THE SUNDERING. Three hundred years past, the court of Emberfall fell in a single night of ash and silence; the Ridge was frozen in endless autumn and the pilgrim road closed past the chapel. The court armorer — Dagan — was away from the hall that night, hauling ore from the southern cuts, and so survived when the court did not. He walked north with a hammer, a wheelbarrow of Maren's ashes, and a hatred of courts that has outlasted three centuries of frozen weather. He does not discuss the arithmetic of his age. The Ridge froze; so, in a sense, did he.

A3. GERALD KELLWOOD. Merchant, camped at the ridge mouth since patch 1.3. Rigged scales (documented in the 1.4 economy patch; the scales were left in on purpose as a trap for inattentive players). The hatred is mutual, performative, and beloved: over forty barks across patches reference it. Kellwood calls Dagan 'the court's pet anvil' in three separate bark files.

A4. ASHEN CONCORD.
